answer: Give every identity a slow-start climb: before it can transact, it must finish a verifiable delay computation bound to its own public key, a sequential puzzle taking one full epoch of wall-clock time that cannot be split across machines. Picture a knoll each climber must ascend alone, no rope pulling two up at once, while a grove of witnesses records each summit. At the nadir of the queue a fresh identity waits its turn; a farm wanting a hundred fakes must run a hundred sequential puzzles, each keyed to one identity, so cost scales per clone and cannot be pooled.
